_source: Fable 5.1's performance direction sheet (verbatim tags/intent/stability). Global: speed 0.9 unless noted; downward cadence on every full stop; if a take sounds sad, it's wrong.

lines.intent: Boredom that is actually grief, hidden well. 'Can' lands flat, not sad.
lines.text: [dry, half to herself] I know this part. [pause] I've read it in forty tongues. Every telling ends on the same page. [a breath] Nobody ever shows. [flat] Nobody ever can.

lines.intent: The one joke she allows herself. 'Hm' is the punchline.
lines.text: ...and the mother tried. [pause] And the mother went sideways. [under her breath, amused] Hm. [pause] Sideways. [dry] And that's where the book ends. [flat] Every time.

lines.intent: Bemused, not a lesson (Michael). "There's no" is a shrug; "there is no" is a verdict (Fable). The half-laugh is at the question, not at her.
lines.text: [amused sigh] Oh, there's no "and then." [fond, half-laughing] That's what an ending is.

lines.intent: A footnote to her chorus. Settling contour.
lines.text: [low, under the music] Every story's borrowed till somebody stands to tell it.

lines.intent: The most honest line she has. The second half barely louder than breath.
lines.text: [dry] I have read how it ends. [a breath] I'd still like to see.

lines.intent: Catching herself moralising. Fast self-correction, then a plain instruction.
lines.text: [quick, dry] That's the moral. [immediately] No, it isn't. [pause] Keep walking.

lines.intent: Conceding the argument without admitting it.
Facts about herself, precisely, to someone she trusts. Quieter and more exact, never wetter.
lines.text: [measured, close] I know how every story ends. [pause] I've read them all: the fox, the crow, the boy who cried, the one who flew too near the sun. [a breath] I know the moral before the page. [flat] That's the job. [pause] You stand in the dark, [slower] and you know.

lines.intent: The admission. Smallest line in the song. The surprise is in the stillness.
lines.text: [a breath] [quiet, exact] ...I didn't know this one.

lines.intent: The narrator has left the book. 'Sorekara?' light, not triumphant.
lines.text: [steady, standing] Mukashi mukashi was a long time ago. [pause] This is now. [a beat, lifting slightly] Sorekara?

lines.intent: An echo a bar behind Clawd. Barely a statement.
Answering her 'why?'. Her one clearly smiling line.
lines.text: [amused, quick] And I'm made of "and then."

lines.intent: The last word of the film, over an open fifth. Certain, unhurried, no smile.
